name: CodeWhale

surfaces.label: Interactive TUI: `codewhale` or its byte-identical alias `codew` (macOS Mach-O arm64/x64, ~64 MiB, installed to ~/.local/bin by https://codewhale.net/install.sh; also Homebrew (`brew install Hmbown/deepseek-tui/codewhale`, macOS formula exists), `cargo install codewhale-cli`, or npm `codewhale`). One binary, TUI runs in-process, one process is one session. The npm bins `codewhale`/`codew` are node shims (argv[0]=node, cannot match) that spawn the native binary `<pkg>/bin/downloads/codewhale` as a direct child with stdio inherit, so only the native process matches. `codewhale-tui` is a compatibility name (a standalone `cargo install codewhale-tui` binary, and the sibling child of the 0.8.41-0.9.4 dispatcher). Non-session subcommands and `exec`, `serve`, `app-server`, `web` are vetoed by exact argument. No .app bundle, so no bundle id. Known limits of the matcher: exclude_args is an exact match against ANY argument, so a prompt that is exactly one listed word (`codewhale review`) is hidden; sessions started with `resume <id>`/`fork <id>` match but the positional id is not read.

`codewhale exec "prompt"` (also `codew exec`): headless one-shot, no caffeinate, no TUI chrome, alive means working. Global flags may come before `exec`. `--resume/--session-id` resume a saved session. Known limit: args_contain is a SUBSTRING test on every argument, so an interactive `codewhale` whose prompt, path or flag value merely contains `exec` (for example `-C ~/executive` or `--model x-exec`) is filed here as one-shot, and one-shot means alive equals working. Tested with agents_probe.matches(); the registry offers no positional match to avoid it (registry/README.md section 3 case 16).

Runtime API host: `codewhale serve --http|--mobile` and `codewhale app-server --http|--mobile` (HTTP/SSE /v1/* on 127.0.0.1:7878, bearer token). One process holds many threads, so no session id in argv and no per-process state. `codewhale web` (local browser client, same runtime, default port 7878), `serve --web|--acp|--mcp`, `app-server --stdio` and legacy `app-server` (8787) are NOT matched: their argv has no distinctive flag and matching bare words would misfile prompts. Matched here by the --http flag only. Same substring limit: a prompt containing the text `--http` is filed as a daemon host.

Legacy DeepSeek TUI (before the 0.8.41 rebrand, 2026-05-23): binary `deepseek-tui`, spawned by the `deepseek` dispatcher as a direct child (confirmed in the v0.8.40 source, crates/cli/src/lib.rs delegate_simple_tui `Command::new(&tui)`; not observed running). The dispatcher itself is not matched because `deepseek` is a name other tools use. Stores in ~/.deepseek/. This binary and every release up to v0.9.13 hold NO caffeinate child (the sleep guard first ships in v0.10.0), so only tree_cpu applies. The subcommand veto list is copied from the current CLI, not from the legacy one.

Codewhale desktop app (native GPUI macOS app, separate repository, development build, no public download as of 2026-09-30). Bundle id and process name unknown, so nothing is matched. It drives the same Runtime API as `serve --http`.

VS Code extension HengQuWorld.brotherwhale-vscode (community maintained, https://github.com/HengQuWorld/CodeWhale-VSCode): a sidebar client of the local Runtime. It ships no agent process of its own that this row can match.
Hosted web app app.codewhale.net (development preview; `/rc` in a terminal session hands it to the web) and `codewhale dispatch` cloud agents. Nothing local to see.

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: Only from v0.10.0 (2026-09-22) on: every earlier release, including all of 0.8.41-0.9.13 and the legacy deepseek-tui, holds no sleep inhibitor and has no such child. The interactive TUI spawns `caffeinate -i` (v0.10.0) or `caffeinate -i -w <own pid>` (main, v0.10.1 candidate) as a direct child for the whole of a turn (guard bound to Engine::run_turn) and kills it when the turn returns. Not held by exec, serve, app-server or web. Inferred from source: it stays held while the turn waits on an approval or a question, so pair it with the waiting signals.

Fallback only. Also the only signal for `exec` and the Runtime API host, where CPU is not proof. Never proves idle: model calls burn none. The 3% floor is the registry default, not measured for this harness; it is the only signal on releases before v0.10.0.

waiting_signals.meaning: Fires when an approval prompt opens, a request_user_input question is shown, or a goal continuation is parked. Needs a [[hooks.hooks]] entry in config.toml. `session_busy` fires when work resumes.
Session settled back to idle after a turn or wait, nothing outstanding.
Exact state per process, opt-in with `[control_socket] enabled = true` (default off). Newline JSON-RPC, one request per connection. The path is per running session and removed with it.
Open-turn record: turn.started without a closing turn.* event. Opt-in, off by default, one file may be shared by many processes.

hooks.config: ~/.codewhale/config.toml `[hooks]` + `[[hooks.hooks]]` (legacy ~/.deepseek/config.toml, or CODEWHALE_CONFIG_PATH); project `<workspace>/.codewhale/hooks.toml` loads only after workspace trust plus `/hooks approve <digest>`. List with `/hooks` in the TUI.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry exporter: Cargo.lock has no opentelemetry crate and grep for OTEL/OTLP finds nothing in crates/ or docs/ (only pet/ and telemetry-ingest/package-lock.json). Product analytics are aggregate batches (no per-turn or per-tool timeline) sent to the first-party ingest at https://telemetry.codewhale.net/v1/telemetry, on by default, off with `codewhale config set telemetry false` or CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY=0. PostHog is an optional downstream sink of that ingest, inert until its operator configures it (docs/TELEMETRY.md), so it is not part of what the client does. An opt-in `[lifecycle_outbox]` writes JSONL and can POST a webhook.

sources.claim: Process patterns: interactive vs exec vs daemon filing, tested with agents_probe.matches() on synthetic argv
sources.evidence: python3 harness importing tools/agents_probe.py, 34 argv. Correct: `codewhale`, `codew`, full path with --resume, -p prompt, resume/fork/rc/run and -c match the TUI surface; doctor, update, review, help, web, deepseek and the node shim match nothing; `codewhale exec`, `--model x exec` match the exec surface; `serve --http`, `app-server --http` match the daemon. Wrong by construction: `codew -C /Users/x/executive` and `codewhale --model exec-model` match the exec (one-shot) surface; `codewhale --workspace model` and `--profile config` (values equal to a vetoed word) match nothing

notes: Nothing was run: CodeWhale is not installed here, so every claim comes from the public repo (main 568abae, tag v0.10.0) and docs. Key facts. (1) One Rust binary, `codewhale`, with `codew` as a byte-identical alias; the old `deepseek`/`deepseek-tui` names are pre-0.8.41. (2) From v0.10.0 the interactive TUI holds a direct-child `caffeinate` for the whole turn, so the standard child_process signal is the most precise working signal; it is TUI-only, so `exec` (oneshot) and the Runtime API host need CPU or an API read. (3) Caffeinate probably stays on during approval waits, so let `waiting_for_user` (hook) or control-socket `turn_state` = waiting override it. (4) The hook session id `sess_xxxxxxxx` (DEEPSEEK_SESSION_ID / CODEWHALE_SESSION_ID) is not the saved-session UUID in the file name. (5) A fresh session has no id in argv, so mapping a process to its <uuid>.json needs lsof on the .late-usage/<id>.live lock, or the control-socket directory name. (6) transcript_write is not listed as a working signal: autosave timing was not established and would extend `working` after a turn ends. (7) With the 0.8.41-0.9.4 dispatcher, `codewhale` is the parent of a `codewhale-tui` child; the outermost-match rule reports the dispatcher, and tree_cpu still sees the child because it sums the whole tree. No release before v0.10.0 holds caffeinate (verified by source diff across tags), so on those installs, and on the legacy deepseek-tui, the only working signal is tree_cpu, which never proves idle. (8) Matcher limits, tested: args_contain is a substring test, so an interactive session with `exec` anywhere in an argument is filed as one-shot (alive equals working), and a prompt containing `--http` is filed as a daemon host; exclude_args is exact, so a prompt that is exactly a vetoed word hides a session. (9) ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json also matches session_boot_owners.json, which is not a session. (10) Telemetry: PostHog is an optional downstream sink of the first-party ingest, not the client endpoint. No args_contain on the caffeinate signal on purpose: v0.10.0 spawns plain `caffeinate -i`, and only main adds `-w <own pid>`, so requiring -w would blind the released version.
